quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, what must you do?

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle, you must turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: What affects your braking distance?

options.text: How fast your vehicle is traveling.
The condition of your brakes and tires.
The condition of the road surface.

questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on how fast you are driving, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road surface.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Make drivers angry about slow traffic.
Keep traffic away from hazardous work areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic away from hazardous work areas.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for both workers and drivers. Look for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests. They warn you and tell you where to go.

questions.question: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop when another driver moves unexpectedly.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds require longer stopping distances. The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop when you need to react to another driver's unexpected movement.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing sign, slow down, look for trains, and be ready to stop. If the red lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not try to go around the gate.

questions.question: If you have drunk several beers, how can you reduce the effects of alcohol?
questions.explanation: Only time will reduce alcohol's effects on your body. Cold showers, coffee, or physical activity will not speed up this process. It takes about one hour for your body to process one drink.

questions.question: You feel angry after a bad day at work. When you reach your car, what should you do?

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the highway to release your anger.
Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive home.
Stop at a bar and have a few drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive home.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, wait before driving. Driving while emotional is dangerous for you and others on the road.

questions.question: Before you start your vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure all passengers buckle their safety belts.

questions.explanation: Develop a habit when getting into your car. Before you start the engine, buckle your safety belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?

options.text: Children do not react as quickly as adults.
Children are smaller and harder to see.

questions.explanation: Children are often unpredictable and hard to see. Be extra careful near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and ice cream trucks. Watch for children on bikes on sidewalks—they may ride into the road suddenly.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the road ahead has a series of turns or curves.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol helps the medicine cure a cold.
The combination can make the effects of both the alcohol and medicine much stronger.
There is no effect because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination can make the effects of both the alcohol and medicine much stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with other drugs can make both drugs affect your body more strongly. For example, one drink plus cold medicine can affect you as much as several drinks without medicine.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.question: When should you change lanes?

options.text: When a car is in your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and carefully. Only change lanes when you need to. Every lane change increases the risk of an accident.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has curves.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians on or crossing the road. Be extra careful where children are present. Always let pedestrians cross in a crosswalk.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing with no warning signals (like flashing lights or gates), should a driver slow down, look, and listen?
questions.explanation: If a railroad crossing has no warning devices or only a crossbuck sign, slow down and look both ways. Listen for trains or railroad equipment. Only cross when it is safe.

questions.question: A traffic light is green, but a police officer signals you to stop. What should you do?

options.text: Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.explanation: You must always obey a police officer, even if they tell you to do something different from the traffic signal or road signs.

questions.question: What should you do if you encounter an aggressive driver?
questions.explanation: The safest thing to do is get out of the way of an aggressive driver. Never compete with other drivers. Always respect other road users.

questions.question: What problems do worn or bald tires cause?
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance, make turning harder, and increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, who must you yield to?
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to all pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: Before entering an intersection, you should look to your:
questions.explanation: Before entering an intersection, look left and right for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians. Look left a second time because vehicles from your left will reach you faster than those from your right. Check across the entire intersection before moving to ensure it is safe.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: All traffic must go straight ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road joins from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a road is joining from the right ahead.

questions.question: In which of the following ways can alcohol affect you?
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. You may feel overly confident or silly. Alcohol also slows your reaction time, harms your coordination and balance, and makes it hard to judge distances. This makes it difficult to react safely.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol from your system?
questions.explanation: Alcohol works quickly but leaves your system slowly. Fresh air, cold showers, and coffee cannot lower your blood alcohol level. Waiting is the only way to reduce it.

questions.question: While getting your driver license, you may:

options.text: Choose to be an organ and tissue donor.

questions.explanation: At age 18 or older, you can choose to be an organ and tissue donor when getting your driver license. Males ages 18-25 will be registered with Selective Service unless they opt out. U.S. citizens who will be 18 by the next election can register to vote or update their registration.
